text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, reversing some of a rough two-week slide that had knocked the stock down nearly 7%. The bounce likely reflects relief after news Friday of potential U.S.-Iran negotiations—geopolitical tension around Iran has been pushing global oil prices higher (currently $123/barrel globally versus $103 domestically), which typically boosts refiner margins, and any hint of de-escalation can ease that premium. The stock may also have found footing after the company announced leadership changes and a company update on October 29th, though the market's initial reaction was to sell first and ask questions later.

The broader context matters here: Big Oil refiners have been caught in a squeeze between high crude costs and investor skepticism. Gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel have all surged despite Trump's campaign promise to cut energy costs, and while that sounds good for refiners' bottom lines in theory, the market has been wary—CNBC noted this week that investors "should be cautious" as Big Oil earnings season arrives. Today's bounce is modest and sits well below where the stock traded just days ago, suggesting investors remain uncertain about what these near-term refining windfalls mean for longer-term returns.
